rules.statement: When a write whose outcome doesn't depend on the state it read (such as revoking a grant) loses an optimistic concurrency race, open a new unit of work, read again and retry, up to a small fixed number of attempts (3 in total), then let the concurrency exception propagate.
rules.why: Without a retry, a lost race leaves the grants active and the endpoint fails (500 instead of RFC 7009's 200). Unbounded retries could livelock, and three attempts are enough because each attempt reads again.
rules.check: Look for revocation-style save paths that catch nothing on a store concurrency exception, or that retry in the same unit of work, without re-reading, or in an unbounded loop.

rules.statement: Put the re-read-and-retry loop for revocations in the central grant service and route every revocation through it, rather than writing the retry in each endpoint or handler.
rules.why: If every caller repeats the loop, a caller that forgets it answers 500 or 412 for a correct revocation.
rules.check: Look for endpoints or handlers that revoke grants directly through a store or unit of work instead of the shared service, or that add their own retry loops around a revocation.

rules.statement: A filter-driven bulk modification or revocation must throw ArgumentException when given an empty filter, and an identifier field added to the filter must be included in its emptiness check.
rules.why: Rejecting an empty filter means an unscoped bulk operation can't happen by accident.
rules.check: Look for bulk operations that take a filter but never check whether it is empty, and for new filter properties that the IsEmpty logic leaves out.

rules.statement: A state transition that happens only once (for example, revoking a single grant) returns whether this call performed it, returning false when the target is unknown, belongs to another tenant, or was already transitioned, including by a concurrent request.
rules.why: Callers need to know whether their own call made the change, so they can react correctly when a concurrent request got there first.
rules.check: Look for once-only operations that return void or throw when the item is missing or already transitioned, instead of reporting a boolean result.

rules.statement: Record an audit event for a modification only when the operation's returned count or result shows that this call actually changed something.
rules.why: If another request revoked the item in between, auditing anyway records the same change twice.
rules.check: Look for audit or event emission that happens after reading the entity but isn't gated on the count or success result the write returned.

rules.statement: Don't blindly retry a spend that requires the grant to still be active (consuming a code, rotating or replacing a token) after it loses a concurrency race. Answer the lost race as a second spend or a reuse.
rules.why: A spend's outcome depends on what it read, so retrying could let a grant be spent twice. Only operations whose outcome doesn't depend on the read state can safely retry.
rules.check: Look for retry-on-concurrency-exception loops around consume, rotate or replace operations that would retry the spend instead of treating it as a replay or reuse.
